documents.title: mapfx.norm: a method for removing unwanted variation from massively parallel cytometry data.
documents.abstract: Massively parallel cytometry (MPC) experiments allow cost-effective quantification of >200 surface proteins at single-cell resolution. The Infinity Flow protocol was developed to measure highly informative protein 'Backbone' markers on all cells in wells distributed across plates, along with well-specific exploratory protein 'Infinity' markers. Backbone markers are then used to impute the Infinity markers using machine learning methods. This protocol offers unprecedented opportunities for more comprehensive classification of cell types. However, the protocol can be improved, particularly in re

documents.title: CoEVFold suite: User friendly pipelines to visually represent protein coevolution.
documents.abstract: Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) data underlies current principles in protein folding and protein-protein interaction prediction, from which deep-learning models trained on protein sequence and structure datasets can predict protein structure. However, what is missing are user-friendly tools that enable researchers to identify and visualise coevolution, the principal signal that these MSAs encode. Here we present tools to identify and visualize coevolution, through a pipeline (CoEVFold) that uses basic direct coupling algorithms derived from GREMLIN and an input alignment of sequences from MM

documents.title: Chemical profiling, bioactivity, and machine learning-supported target analysis of Euphorbia macroclada extracts from aerial parts and roots.
documents.abstract: Euphorbia macroclada is used in Anatolian folk medicine, but its chemistry and bioactivity have not been compared across plant parts and extraction solvents. We extracted aerial parts and roots with ethyl acetate, acetone, 70% aqueous acetone and water. The extracts were then profiled by LC-MS/MS and tested in antioxidant and enzyme inhibition assays. UHPLC-ESI-Orbitrap-MS/MS analysis showed 101 compounds, mainly flavonoids, hydrolysable tannins, coumarins, and phenolic acid derivatives. The aqueous acetone extracts had the highest phenolic content (up to 86.94 mg GAE per g, roots) and the str

documents.title: Association of Estimated Insulin Sensitivity With Cardiovascular Disease in Individuals Without Diabetes: Use of Traditional and Machine Learning.
documents.abstract: The predictive role of the Estimated Insulin Sensitivity (e-IS) index, serving as a surrogate marker for insulin resistance, in cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mechanisms remains underexplored in nondiabetic populations. We aimed to evaluate the association of e-IS with CVD incidence and its predictive utility for CVD risk.

documents.title: Natural Language Processing Supported by Annotation Process Artifacts to Detect Risky Alcohol Use in Electronic Health Records: Algorithm Development and Validation Study.
documents.abstract: High-risk alcohol use and alcohol use disorder (AUD) are significant contributors to surgical risk and complications yet remain underidentified in surgical populations. While electronic health records (EHRs) contain relevant information about patients' alcohol use in clinical notes, manual chart review is time-intensive and impractical at scale. Natural language processing (NLP) offers a path to automated identification, but alcohol-related risk classes are highly imbalanced in clinical populations, making multiclass classification particularly challenging.

documents.title: RNAcomp2D: a web tool to execute multiple methods and visually compare predictions of RNA secondary structure.
documents.abstract: Ribonucleic acids (RNAs) are involved in many important biological processes. In particular, non-coding RNAs are crucial regulators of cellular processes, playing a significant role in gene expression. RNA secondary structure is key to infer their specific function and for understanding how they interact with other molecules. Many computational models have been developed in the last decade to predict the secondary structure, achieving increasingly higher success rates. However, each new method has its own input-output interface, programming language, computational requirements and, sometimes,

documents.title: DNNGP-Pro: A multi-omics data integration platform for predictive modeling of complex traits and crop hybrid breeding.
documents.abstract: Accurate prediction of complex agronomic traits poses a long-standing challenge for hybrid crop breeding, which may be resolved by integrating multi-omics data with shared-parent relationship information among hybrids. To accelerate variety development, we constructed the DNNGP-Pro platform for predictive modeling of complex hybrid traits in large-scale populations. In preliminary steps, the pipeline extracts local features from omics data via convolutional neural networks, then employs graph convolutional networks to integrate these single-omics features with hybrid shared-parent graph (HSPG)

documents.title: Integrated Whole-Cell Phage Display and Machine Learning Identify Candidate Targeting Ligands in KRAS-Defined Lung Cancer Contexts.
documents.abstract: Phage display can identify ligands that target distinctive cell surface phenotypes, but selection outputs are often complex and difficult to interpret. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining phage display biopanning, next-generation sequencing (NGS), machine learning (ML), and flow cytometry to discover short peptide binders associated with genotype-defined cancer contexts. Phage display was performed on lung cancer cell lines representing KRAS wild-type (WT), G12C, G12D, and G12V backgrounds, and experimental outputs were used to train a multimodal probabilistic model. From the r

documents.title: An EFHD1-associated ADSC niche modulates treatment response in experimental models of ER-positive breast cancer.
documents.abstract: Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) modulate the breast cancer (BC) microenvironment, but their role in endocrine therapy resistance and clinical outcomes remains ill-defined.

documents.title: A dendritic cell-related prognostic signature in glioma: A multi-omic framework integrating transcriptomics, single-cell profiling, and clinical validation.
documents.abstract: Dendritic cells (DCs) infiltrating the glioma microenvironment can promote antitumor immunity or contribute to immunosuppression and immune escape. This dual role underscores the need to define dendritic cell-related genes (DCRGs) for prognostic assessment. Using transcriptomic and clinical data from glioma cohorts (The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA)), combined with scRNA-seq analysis, we identified ten pivotal DCRGs (CASP1, CD300LF, CTSB, GPR132, HLA-DQA1, PLCB2, RAC2, SIGLEC9, STAT6, TLR1) associated with patient outcomes. A DCRG-based risk signature, devel

documents.title: Unsupervised Deep Learning for Cryo-EM/ET Particle Classification.
documents.abstract: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is widely used to determine protein structures from purified samples. With cryogenic electron tomography (cryo-ET), it is possible to image thin sections of cells and directly visualize diverse proteins in their native environment. However, separating the massive mixture of different types of proteins inside cells remains challenging, especially without human intervention. In this work, we present an unsupervised deep learning framework for classifying cryo-EM/ET particle images that jointly optimizes for pose and structure through an autoencoder-based m
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: sorAI - a suite of machine learning models to predict plant polyploidy from target capture data.
documents.abstract: Polyploidy is a persistent feature of land plant evolution, yet it is often difficult to determine the ploidy of individual plants. The growing abundance of target capture data and other high throughput sequence datasets across plant species has generated interest in methods to infer ploidy from these data. We leverage chromosome count data and target capture data from the GoFlag probe set in ferns to train new machine learning models to infer if a sample is from a diploid or polyploid genome.
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Unraveling the genetic architecture of the human mammillary bodies.
documents.abstract: The mammillary bodies are a central component of the hippocampal-diencephalic-cingulate network that is critically involved in emotion processing and memory function, yet their genetic architecture remains unknown. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of mammillary body volume in 38,064 participants from the UK Biobank and replicated our findings in the Rhineland Study cohort (N = 4,860). Mammillary body and hypothalamic subregional volumes were derived from structural brain MRIs using FastSurfer-HypVINN, an established and validated deep learning-based segmentation tool. Univar
documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: stem.MAP: Identification of cell-type-specific protein complexes in mammalian embryonic stem cells.
documents.abstract: Protein complexes carry out critical functions during development. Mapping cell-type-specific protein complexes in early embryogenesis is essential for uncovering the molecular mechanisms of embryonic development. We unfortunately currently lack a catalog of protein complexes specific for embryogenesis including embryonic stem cells. Here we develop a proteomics-based machine learning workflow to predict protein complexes present in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESC). Our method integrates data from a cell-type agnostic protein complex resource with co-fractionation mass spectrometry (CF-MS) ex
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions.
documents.abstract: Malignant effusions are clinically accessible yet underutilized sources of metastatic tumor cells. However, abundant background immune cells complicate tumor cell isolation and molecular characterization. We integrate AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free tumor cell enrichment with genomic profiling to characterize phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions.
documents.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

documents.title: Synthetic MPRA perturbation supervision improves variant-effect prediction in sequence-to-function models.
documents.abstract: Deep learning sequence-to-function (S2F) models learn to predict functional readouts, such as gene expression, from genetic sequence. However, these models are trained predominantly on the reference genome and struggle to accurately predict the effect of genetic variation on gene expression. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) explore the direct impact of genetic variation on gene expression, but saturation-mutagenesis MPRAs that measure variant effects directly remain limited, thereby restricting their use for fine-tuning S2F models. In this work, we investigate fine-tuning Borzoi, a s
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Predicting single-molecule chromatin distribution from DNA sequence.
documents.abstract: Genome regulation unfolds through dynamic and stochastic single-molecule events. Deep learning models that read gene regulatory activities from DNA sequences have markedly advanced our ability to predict cell-population-level averages. However, they cannot capture the full spectrum of heterogeneity and dynamics at the single-molecule level, which directly reflect the underlying mechanisms of genome regulation. Here, we introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) framework that directly models the entire probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states from DNA sequence alone. We u
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: EV Barcode: A Machine Learning Driven Web Resource for Predicting the Cellular Origin of Extracellular Vesicles From Protein and mRNA Cargo.
documents.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membranous particles secreted by most cell types into the extracellular space, carrying proteins, RNAs, metabolites, and lipids that reflect the physiological state of their cell of origin. Hence, EVs are considered as powerful resource of non-invasive biomarkers for disease diagnosis and prognosis. However, identifying the cellular source of EVs in complex biological samples including blood, urine and milk remains a major challenge, limiting clinical and biological insights. To address this, we developed EV Barcode (https://evbarcode.org/), an open-source web

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Precision Nanomedicine: Bridging Delivery Barriers, Controlled Release, and Clinical Translation.
documents.abstract: Targeted drug delivery aims to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity, yet its clinical translation remains limited by the unpredictable in vivo behaviour of nanocarriers. Although a broad range of nanocarrier platforms-including lipid-, polymer-, protein-, inorganic- and biomimetic-based systems-can improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, lesion-site accumulation and controlled release, their performance is frequently constrained by heterogeneous disease biology, insufficient tissue penetration, premature clearance, immune recognition and manufacturing variability.

documents.title: Integrative multi-omics, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation reveal PFAS-associated immune-inflammatory signatures in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
documents.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders. However, the systems-level connections among PFAS-associated molecular perturbations, immune dysregulation, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to prioritize candidate links between PFAS-associated target information and COPD-related transcriptional and inflammatory signatures.

documents.title: Physiological proxies of feed efficiency in pigs: exploring the predictive value of blood biochemical and hematological profiles.
documents.abstract: Developing strategies to improve feed efficiency can help the swine industry become more sustainable while meeting the worldwide demand for pork products, yet most commercial barns cannot practically calculate direct metrics of individual feed efficiency. Physiological indicators of metabolic pathways can serve as intermediate variables to predict performance outcomes and, therefore, as biomarkers of feed efficiency and other desirable production traits in growing pigs. This research aimed to assess the role of conventional blood parameters as proxies for performance outcomes and their predict

documents.title: Integrative ferroptosis-related bioinformatics identifies PPARγ as a therapeutic target of ursolic acid against inflammation and pathological osteogenesis in ankylosing spondylitis.
documents.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease characterized by persistent inflammation and aberrant new bone formation. Ferroptosis has increasingly been implicated in immune dysregulation and pathological bone remodeling; however, its molecular involvement in AS and its potential value for natural product discovery remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify ferroptosis-related molecular targets in AS, screen natural compounds targeting the key candidate, and validate their therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms.
documents.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

documents.title: Medical-oriented multi-label diagnosis of twelve-lead ECG signals via disease-aware relational modeling and pathology-aware temporal evidence aggregation.
documents.abstract: Twelve-lead ECG signals are of great value in cardiovascular disease screening and assisted diagnosis, but their multi-label recognition process is simultaneously affected by cross-lead structural dependencies, disease label co-occurrence relationships, and the dispersed distribution of pathological evidence in long-sequence signals. To address these issues, this study proposes a deep learning model for twelve-lead ECG multi-label diagnosis. The model adopts a Transformer-Mamba hybrid structure as the temporal encoding backbone to extract local waveform variations and long-range rhythm feature

documents.title: Machine learning prediction of 1-year thrombosis risk in membranous nephropathy: integration of renal pathology and early longitudinal trajectories.
documents.abstract: Patients with membranous nephropathy (MN) have an increased risk of thrombotic events. Existing prediction approaches primarily use clinical and laboratory measurements obtained at a single time point and rarely incorporate renal pathology or early longitudinal changes. This study integrated multiple types of information to predict the occurrence of thrombosis from 4 weeks after discharge to 1 year after being diagnosed with MN.

documents.title: A machine learning-assisted hypoxia-associated prognostic model reveals PFKP-mediated glycolytic regulation in uveal melanoma.
documents.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is a highly aggressive intraocular malignancy with strong metastatic propensity and poor response to immunotherapy. Hypoxia profoundly reshapes the tumor microenvironment and drives immune evasion. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-assisted hypoxia-related prognostic model and identify relevant metabolic candidates associated with UM progression.

documents.title: Predicting Translation Readthrough from Sequence Features in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
documents.abstract: Understanding translation readthrough in eukaryotes is fundamental for elucidating transcript evolution, deciphering gene expression codes, and advancing biotechnological applications. In this study, we present the first comprehensive analysis of the transcript features that determine readthrough efficiency in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. To predict readthrough efficiency, we engineered a set of novel sequence-derived features and trained multiple machine learning models, achieving a mean Spearman correlation of 0.535 between predicted and experimentally measured values, substantially improving p

documents.title: Prediction of multi-stage Alzheimer's disease progression based on surface-based morphometry and machine learning.
documents.abstract: Early identification of individuals at high risk of progression from normal cognition (NC) to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and from MCI to Alzheimer's disease (AD) is crucial for timely intervention. However, predictive models that simultaneously address multiple transition stages along the AD continuum remain limited.

documents.title: Explainable volumetric deep learning from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI for preoperative IDH prediction in adult-type diffuse gliomas: a two-center study.
documents.abstract: To evaluate contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI (CE-T1WI) models for preoperative prediction of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status in adult-type diffuse gliomas and explore phenotype associations of influential latent features.
